skill.name: claude-code-hooks
skill.description: Guides users in configuring Claude Code hooks for tool validation, audit logging, approvals, session setup, and safer hook scripts.
skill.summary: Configure Claude Code hooks for validation, logging, approvals, and secure automation.
skill.author: 0xDarkMatter

security_audit.summary: The package is documentation-only, and most static alerts are Markdown examples for Claude Code hook configuration, defensive blocklists, or official documentation links. I confirmed risk around examples that source .env.local at session start and semantic privacy risks from unredacted hook input logging. No prompt injection language was found in the reviewed files.

remediation.issue: SessionStart example sources a project .env.local file.
remediation.suggestion: Do not source project environment files directly. Use a dotenv parser, whitelist allowed keys, and require explicit opt-in for secret loading.

remediation.issue: Audit logging examples persist complete hook input or tool_input.
remediation.suggestion: Log only sanitized metadata by default. Redact prompts, file contents, command arguments, tokens, and environment values before writing logs.

remediation.issue: Examples include broad matchers and global settings paths.
remediation.suggestion: Prefer project-local settings, narrow matchers, explicit script paths, and short timeouts for production hook workflows.

remediation.issue: Copied shell examples depend on user hardening.
remediation.suggestion: Show complete production examples with strict shell options, jq error handling, path allowlists, and dependency checks.

content.value_statement: Claude Code teams need predictable controls before and after tool execution. This skill explains hook events, matcher patterns, settings, and safer script patterns.
actual_capabilities: Explains Claude Code hook events and when each event runs.
Shows settings locations, matcher patterns, hook commands, and timeout options.
Documents PreToolUse and PostToolUse patterns for validation and logging.
Describes hook script inputs, exit codes, and jq-based parsing.
Provides security patterns for path checks, command guards, rate limits, and permissions.
Includes troubleshooting steps for hook loading and manual script tests.
limitations: It is documentation only and does not install ready-made hook scripts.
It requires Claude Code CLI support for hooks and settings files.
Most examples assume a Unix shell and the jq command-line tool.
User-created hooks still need local security review before deployment.

use_cases.title: Guard risky commands
use_cases.description: Create PreToolUse checks that block dangerous Bash commands or unsafe file paths.

use_cases.title: Add tool audit trails
use_cases.description: Configure PostToolUse logging for tool activity while planning safe redaction rules.

use_cases.title: Standardize project hooks
use_cases.description: Set local hook settings, matchers, and timeouts for repeatable team workflows.

prompt_templates.title: List Available Events
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain the Claude Code hook events in this skill. Recommend the event I should use for validating a file write.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Hook Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me plan a PreToolUse hook that validates Bash commands. Include matcher choice, exit behavior, timeout, and test steps.

prompt_templates.title: Review Hook Configuration
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my Claude Code hook configuration for scope, matcher accuracy, path safety, timeout values, and logging risk.

prompt_templates.title: Design Secure Hook Controls
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a secure hook workflow with command blocking, sanitized audit logging, rate limiting, and project-local settings.

output_examples.input: A developer wants Claude Code to stop risky shell commands before execution.
output_examples.output: The skill outlines a PreToolUse hook plan with a Bash matcher, blocking exit behavior, and command validation checks.

output_examples.input: A team needs a record of AI tool activity across projects.
output_examples.output: The skill describes PostToolUse audit logging patterns and explains why logs should keep sanitized metadata only.

output_examples.input: A platform engineer needs project-specific hook settings.
output_examples.output: The skill explains global and local settings priority, matcher patterns, hook paths, and timeout configuration.

best_practices: Use project-local settings and narrow matchers when a hook only needs one tool.
Quote variables, validate JSON, and reject path traversal before running hook logic.
Log sanitized metadata instead of prompts, file contents, commands, or secrets.
anti_patterns: Do not use wildcard matchers for sensitive hooks without a clear need.
Do not source project environment files during session startup without a whitelist.
Do not persist complete hook inputs or tool outputs in audit logs.

faq.question: Does this skill install hook scripts automatically?
faq.answer: No. It explains hook configuration and script patterns that users can adapt.

faq.question: Which Claude Code setting files does it cover?
faq.answer: It covers global settings and project-local settings, including their priority relationship.

faq.question: Can hooks block tool execution?
faq.answer: Yes. PreToolUse hooks can block operations by returning the documented blocking exit code.

faq.question: Does it support audit logging?
faq.answer: Yes. It describes PostToolUse logging patterns, but logs should be redacted before production use.

faq.question: What tools do the examples assume?
faq.answer: The examples mainly assume Bash, jq, Claude Code settings, and Unix-like file paths.

faq.question: Is this skill safe for production use as written?
faq.answer: It needs review before production use because copied hook examples can access secrets or create sensitive logs.
